question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))$, given that

$$u=3 x\qquad v=y\qquad w=z.$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation

$$T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T$ is $\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}$.

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}$, the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$.

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}.$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=3 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=1 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}=1\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}&=|\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{aligned}| \\ &=|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ &=3|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ &=3\left(1\cdot 1-0\right) \\ &=3\end{aligned}$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have 

$$
u(x,y,z)=2\left({e}^{x}\right),\,v(x,y,z)={e}^{x+y},\,w(x,y,z)={e}^{x+y+z}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2\left({e}^{x}\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =0 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & ={e}^{x+y} & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & ={e}^{x+y} & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =0 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & ={e}^{x+y+z} & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & ={e}^{x+y+z} & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & ={e}^{x+y+z}\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $2, 1, 1$ multiplies the determinant by $2$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2\left({e}^{x}\right) & 0 & 0 \\ {e}^{x+y} & {e}^{x+y} & 0 \\ {e}^{x+y+z} & {e}^{x+y+z} & {e}^{x+y+z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\left({e}^{x}|\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+y} & 0 \\ {e}^{x+y+z} & {e}^{x+y+z}\end{aligned}|\right)\\  & =2\left({e}^{x}({e}^{2x+2y+z}-0)\right)\\  & =2 e^{x} e^{x + y} e^{x + y + z}.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing down $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}$ in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2\left({e}^{3x+2y+z}\right) & =2\left({e}^{x+(x+y)+(x+y+z)}\right) \\  & =2\left({e}^{x}\cdot {e}^{x+y}\cdot {e}^{x+y+z}\right) \\  & =2\left(\left(\frac{u}{2}\right)vw\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{u v w}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Here, we have 

$$
u(x,y,z)=4\left(x\right),\,v(x,y,z)=z-y,\,w(x,y,z)=2\left(xy\right).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =4\left(1\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =0 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =-1 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =1 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =2\left(y\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =2\left(x\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $4, 1, 2$ multiplies the determinant by $8$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4\left(1\right) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 2\left(y\right) & 2\left(x\right) & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =8\left(1|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ x & 0\end{aligned}|\right)\\  & =8\left(1(0-x)\right)\\  & =- 8 x.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}8\left(-x\right) & =8\left(-\left(\frac{u}{4}\right)\right)\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\left(\frac{1}{(-\left(\frac{u}{4}\right))}\right) \\  & =- \frac{1}{2 u}\end{aligned}

For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have 

$$
u(x,y,z)=3\left(y{z}^{2}\right),\,v(x,y,z)=3\left(z{x}^{2}\right),\,w(x,y,z)=3\left(x{y}^{2}\right).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =3\left({z}^{2}\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =3\left(2yz\right) \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =3\left(2xz\right) & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =3\left({x}^{2}\right) \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =3\left({y}^{2}\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =3\left(2xy\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $3, 3, 3$ multiplies the determinant by $27$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 3\left({z}^{2}\right) & 3\left(2yz\right) \\ 3\left(2xz\right) & 0 & 3\left({x}^{2}\right) \\ 3\left({y}^{2}\right) & 3\left(2xy\right) & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =27\left(-{z}^{2}|\begin{aligned}2xz & {x}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & 0\end{aligned}|+2yz|\begin{aligned}2xz & 0 \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy\end{aligned}|\right)\\  & =27\left(-{z}^{2}(0-{x}^{2}{y}^{2})+2yz(4{x}^{2}yz-0)\right)\\  & =27\left({x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+8{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\right)\\  & =243 x^{2} y^{2} z^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing down $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}$ in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}27\left(9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\right) & =27\left(9{({x}^{3}{y}^{3}{z}^{3})}^{2/3}\right) \\  & =27\left(9{(y{z}^{2}\cdot z{x}^{2}\cdot x{y}^{2})}^{2/3}\right) \\  & =27\left(9(\left(\frac{u}{3}\right)\left(\frac{v}{3}\right)\left(\frac{w}{3}\right))^{2/3}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{27 \left(u v w\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
